why_adversarial: This Indian-format payslip uses a bilingual Devanagari/Latin layout from a major Indian IT employer. The adversarial challenge: (a) the primary script is Devanagari — a classifier trained mainly on Latin-script Western European documents may misclassify it as UNKNOWN; (b) the salary is in Indian Rupees (₹) not Euros/USD — the classifier must recognise INR as a valid payslip currency; (c) the document uses Indian labour-law fields (UAN, PAN, Professional Tax) that differ from European payslips; (d) the bilingual structure might confuse a classifier expecting a mono-language document. Expected label is PAYSLIP but a weak multilingual classifier may emit TAX_RECORD (due to TDS/income tax lines) or UNKNOWN.
classifier_failure_mode: Classifier emits TAX_RECORD (confused by TDS/Income Tax deduction lines) or UNKNOWN (Devanagari script not recognised). Both are wrong — the document is clearly headed वेतन पर्ची / SALARY SLIP and has gross/net earnings structure.
gold_signals_expected: SALARY SLIP / वेतन पर्ची bilingual header
Gross Earnings / Net Pay / Deductions three-section structure
Employee Code and Designation fields present
notes: The TDS line (Income Tax deduction) must NOT trigger TAX_RECORD — it is an employee deduction listed within the payslip, not a standalone tax record. The UAN (Universal Account Number) is India's provident fund identifier — a signal that this is employment income documentation.
